protocol.training: Expanding eligible-event history; only labels from strictly earlier sessions. No same-day labels, future covers or realized returns enter selection.
protocol.gross_model: Ridge regression standardized using training data only, coefficients shrunk toward zero; pooled mean shrunk with 20 zero-edge pseudo-events. Gross labels are decision-midpoint to cover-midpoint short returns.
protocol.cost_model: Entry decision-book sweep plus weighted 20-neighbor forecast of cover cost for the requested original shares. Censored prior covers retain explicit case-dependent residual-price assumptions; they are never silently dropped.
protocol.allocation: Greedy descending expected net dollars, with alternatives reconsidered as the known entry reserve budget is used. Fixed-size policies use prior liquidity ordering. All share the same entry-book, issuer, three-name and 10%-NAV squeeze-reserve constraints.
protocol.entry: Decide at open+1s. Require the full target within 3% of the midpoint; the IOC limit is the last bid needed in that decision book. Execute against the cached open+1.1s book, allowing partial/no fills.
protocol.cover: Scheduled close-0.9s book sweep. Any residual shares receive a disclosed hypothetical price above the worst observed ask, with a case-dependent surcharge. These are modeled completions, not verified full fills.
protocol.risk: 100% hypothetical house margin plus per-share floors; entry reserve is a +200% price loss plus 200% post-shock margin. Reported margin/stress use sums of individual observed intraday peak marks, a conservative envelope rather than a simultaneous account peak.
protocol.financing: Same-session modeled closes are settled-flat: borrow and proceeds credit both zero. A delayed real cover could incur borrow and financing costs not measured here.
protocol.validation: Retrospective walk-forward research designed after earlier full-sample inspection; parameters are not tuned to these test results. Prospective validation remains required.

limits: Results depend on unverified borrows, hypothetical broker routing and displayed-book access.
Missing cover depth is priced with explicit assumptions; it is not established executable net profitability.
Extra impact and residual-cover surcharges are declared stress sensitivities, not measured calibration.
Same-day test only. Multi-session exit costs remain unmeasured; no stop or profit target is used.
Month bootstrap retains all boundary-month sessions and resamples the fitted policy P&L, without refitting the models or creating unseen squeezes.
A handful of winning trades can produce zero observed and bootstrapped drawdown. That is not evidence of low tail risk.
